features.feature_selection#

For this type of exploratory analysis, a good workflow is:

Min-Max normalize all features (mainly useful for visualization and some distance measures). Compute the correlation matrix among features to detect redundancy. Cluster highly correlated features. Compute correlation of each feature with GLC. Optionally aggregate results by the feature groups (ppg_p1_*, ppg_p2_*, etc.).

Note that Pearson correlation is scale-invariant, so Min-Max normalization does not change the correlation coefficients themselves. It mainly helps plots and distance-based methods.

Using: https://pypi.org/project/mrmr-selection/

features.feature_selection.compute_variance_decomposition(features_df: pandas.DataFrame, feature_column: str = 'ppg_entropy', id_column: str = 'participant_id') → dict#

Computes the variance decomposition and Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) for a feature measured repeatedly on participants.

Parameters:

  • features_df (pandas.DataFrame) – DataFrame containing the feature and participant IDs.

  • feature_column (str) – Name of the feature column.

  • id_column (str) – Name of the participant ID column.

Returns:

n_subjects n_observations between_variance within_variance total_variance ICC
